propositions.text: The principal female claimant and her spouse are Israeli citizens originally from the former USSR.
propositions.quote: The principal female claimant, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, and her spouse, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, are citizens of Israel and were originally from the former USSR.

propositions.text: The claimants allege they are Convention refugees and persons in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimants allege that they are "Convention refugees" and "persons in need of protection" under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimants are Israeli citizens from the USSR; the claimants allege refugee status under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The claimants are Jews born in the USSR who left in 1990 and were Russian citizens then.
propositions.quote: The claimants are Jews who were born in the USSR. They left the USSR in 1990, before the fall of the Soviet regime in 1991. They were Russian citizens at the time.

paragraphs.summary: The claimants are Jews born in the USSR who left in 1990 and were Russian citizens then, says the court.

propositions.text: The principal female claimant alleges anti-Semitic attacks and seeking refuge in Israel.
propositions.quote: The principal female claimant alleges that she was subjected to anti-Semitic attacks and that she and her family sought refuge in Israel.

paragraphs.summary: The principal female claimant alleges anti-Semitic attacks and seeking refuge in Israel, says the applicant.

propositions.text: Upon arrival in Israel in 1991, they met an Arab family who helped them, including driving them to a bomb shelter.
propositions.quote: When they arrived in that country, they met an Arab family, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, in 1991. This family drove them to a bomb shelter in XXXXX 1991 and continued to help them afterward.

paragraphs.summary: Upon arrival in Israel in 1991, they met an Arab family who helped them, says the applicant.

propositions.text: After the 2000 Intifada started, the Arab friend was attacked by Israelis; the female claimant tried to protect him but was threatened.
propositions.quote: After the start of the Intifada of 2000, XXXXX was attacked by some Israelis. The female claimant tried to protect him, but she was threatened.

propositions.text: When the female claimant was pushed, her husband and son-in-law came out to protect her.
propositions.quote: When the female claimant XXXXX was pushed, her husband and her son-in-law came out to protect her.

paragraphs.summary: After 2000 Intifada, the Arab friend was attacked; the female claimant tried to protect him but was threatened, says the applicant.

propositions.text: The female claimant alleges repeated insults by neighbours who called police when the Arab friend visited; hostility increased during 2006 Lebanon war.
propositions.quote: The female claimant alleged that she was insulted repeatedly by the neighbours who called the police whenever XXXXX and his family came to visit. During the war with Lebanon in 2006, hostility against the Arabs increased even more.

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant alleges repeated insults by neighbours and increased hostility during 2006 Lebanon war, says the applicant.

propositions.text: In 2007, the female claimant and family were with their Arab friends when neighbours attacked the Arab friend, who was beaten by many men.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX, 2007, the female claimant and her family went to the suburbs with the family of their friend XXXXX. While the men were playing volleyball, they noticed one of their neighbours going towards Mr. XXXXX and pushing him roughly. The latter fell to the ground and XXXXX tried to help him but a large number of men then started to hit him.

paragraphs.summary: In 2007, neighbours attacked the Arab friend while the female claimant and family were present, says the applicant.

propositions.text: The Arab friend was hospitalized and his spouse went to police but they received no help.
propositions.quote: XXXXX had to be taken to the hospital while his spouse went to a police station. She stated that they did not receive any help whatsoever.

paragraphs.summary: The Arab friend was hospitalized and police gave no help, says the applicant.

propositions.text: They called their daughter in Montréal and decided to claim refugee protection in Canada, entering in 2007 and claiming on June 4.
propositions.quote: They telephoned their daughter XXXXX who lives in Montréal and decided to claim refugee protection in that country. They entered the country on XXXXX, 2007, and claimed refugee protection on June 4 of the same year.

paragraphs.summary: They called their daughter in Montréal and claimed refugee protection in Canada in 2007, says the applicant.

propositions.text: After reviewing evidence, the panel determines claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: After analyzing the documentary and testimonial evidence, the panel determines that the claimants are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection".

paragraphs.summary: The panel determines claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection, says the court.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to claimants' identities based on passports, visas, and birth certificates.
propositions.quote: Considering the documents submitted as evidence, namely the photocopies of the claimants' Israeli passports, which are valid from XXXXX, 2003, to XXXXX, 2013, their American visas issued on XXXXX, 2007, which are valid for ten years, their birth certificates issued on XXXXX, 1944, for the female claimant, and on XXXXX, 1980 for the male claimant, the panel is satisfied as to the claimants' identities.

paragraphs.summary: The panel is satisfied as to claimants' identities based on passports, visas, and birth certificates, says the court.

propositions.text: The panel finds the alleged abuse is harassment, not serious enough to be persecution.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the abuse alleged by the claimants is more in keeping with harassment and is not serious enough to be considered persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the alleged abuse is harassment, not serious enough to be persecution, says the court.

propositions.text: Claimants faced harassment in Israel due to not being Jewish, including condescending treatment and police identity checks.
propositions.quote: In fact, during their stay in Israel, the claimants were undoubtedly subjected to harassment from the Jewish society because they were not Jewish. The incidents that they fear should they return consist of condescending treatment towards them by the population in general because of their Russian origin and their Christianity. They also fear the attitude of some police officers when they conduct identity checks.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants faced harassment in Israel due to not being Jewish, including condescending treatment and police checks, says the court.

propositions.text: The female claimant mentioned neighbours left garbage and harassed by calling police repeatedly.
propositions.quote: The female claimant, XXXXX XXXXX, mentioned a few incidents that took place with the neighbours and relates that, among other incidents, the neighbours left garbage, including dog hair and other junk on their doorstep. She also added that the neighbours harassed them by continually telephoning the police.

propositions.text: The female claimant said police checked papers three times but did not add anything else.
propositions.quote: However, when she was questioned about this, she stated that this happened three times and that the police simply checked their papers and did not add anything else.

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant said neighbours harassed by leaving garbage and calling police; police only checked papers thrice, says court and applicant.

propositions.text: The male claimant said a neighbour pushed him once in a park, causing a wrist sprain.
propositions.quote: The claimant XXXXX XXXXX stated that a neighbour pushed him once in a park, when he was with an Arabic family who were friends of his, and he sprained his wrist.

propositions.text: The panel finds these acts unpleasant but not serious abuse.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that these acts are definitely unpleasant, but that they do not qualify as serious abuse.

paragraphs.summary: The male claimant said a neighbour pushed him once causing injury; panel finds acts unpleasant but not serious abuse, says applicant and court.

propositions.text: Persecution requires serious hardship and infringement on fundamental rights, per jurisprudence and Supreme Court in Ward.
propositions.quote: In fact, in order to consider actual or anticipated mistreatment as persecution, it must constitute serious hardship. To determine the severity of an anticipated prejudice, the panel must analyze whether the incidents feared by the claimants constitute an infringement on fundamental rights, as much in the existence of these rights, as in their enjoyment, their expression or their exercise.1 This analysis was supported by the Supreme Court in Ward,2 where the following definition is given for persecution: "sustained or systemic violation of basic human rights demonstrative of a failure of state protection".

propositions.text: Claimants have not proven violation of fundamental rights.
propositions.quote: The claimants have not proven that one or more of their fundamental rights had been violated.

paragraphs.summary: Persecution requires serious hardship and rights violation; claimants have not proven rights violation, says the court.

propositions.text: Claimants' feared treatment does not amount to persecution despite difficulties in Israel.
propositions.quote: The treatment that the claimants fear is not of a degree that could lead to the conclusion that their fear of persecution is well-founded, even though their lives in Israel might have been difficult at times.

propositions.text: The cumulative treatment experienced and feared does not constitute persecution.
propositions.quote: However, the panel is of the opinion that the treatment experienced by the claimants in Israel, and that they fear should they return-even considering the cumulative effect of the actions taken against them-does not constitute persecution.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants' feared treatment does not amount to persecution; cumulative treatment does not constitute persecution, says the court.

propositions.text: Claimants did not use available recourse in Israel before coming to Canada.
propositions.quote: Among other things, the panel is of the opinion that the claimants did not make use of the recourse that was available to them in their country before coming to Canada to claim refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants did not use available recourse in Israel before coming to Canada, says the court.

propositions.text: The female claimant's testimony about filing a police complaint was vague and lacked detail.
propositions.quote: The female claimant's testimony was vague and did not contain much detail.

propositions.text: She eventually said police took notes and asked for name and address but did not request a copy of complaint.
propositions.quote: she eventually mentioned, although only in reply to questions by the panel, that the police took notes and that they asked for her name and address. When asked whether she had requested a copy of her complaint, she stated that she did not think of it because she was worried about her husband.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe she filed a complaint due to lack of corroborating documents and vague testimony.
propositions.quote: The panel does not believe that the female claimant filed a complaint, since she is at pains to explain how she did so and she did not submit any corroborating document, even though she entered Canada on XXXXX, 2007, almost three years ago, which would have given her adequate time to do so.

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant's testimony about filing a police complaint was vague; panel does not believe she filed a complaint, says the court.

propositions.text: The female claimant said she consulted a lawyer who did nothing and said it was not worth the trouble.
propositions.quote: When asked whether she had contacted any other organization to file a complaint, she stated that she consulted a lawyer, but she had difficulty in giving his name. She eventually stated that it was XXXXX XXXXX. When asked what he had allegedly done, she stated that he did nothing, that he simply said that it was not worth the trouble.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the consultation with the lawyer took place as no support or advice was given.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that if the claimants had consulted a lawyer, it is plausible that he would have offered more support or at least told them about the ombudsman, which does not appear to have been the case. The panel does not believe that this consultation took place.

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant said she consulted a lawyer who did nothing; panel does not believe the consultation took place, says the court.

propositions.text: The panel questioned the female claimant about the ombudsman and described the organization's founding and purpose.
propositions.quote: The panel questioned the female claimant about the ombudsman, and mentioned that the organization was founded in 1971 and that it is there to help citizens.

propositions.text: The document states the Office of the Ombudsman was created to examine complaints from all society strata, especially vulnerable groups like new immigrants.
propositions.quote: Office of the Ombudsman was created in order to "examine complaints from every stratum of society," particularly from more vulnerable groups such as new immigrants...

propositions.text: Other organizations offer services to settle new immigrants in many languages.
propositions.quote: Other organizations, such as the Association for Civil Rights in Israel and Israel's Ministry of Immigrant Absorption offer a number of services to settle newly arrived immigrants in many languages.

paragraphs.summary: The panel questioned the claimant about the ombudsman and cited a document describing its role and other immigrant support organizations.

propositions.text: The female claimant is not familiar with the ombudsman and did not file a complaint about alleged threats.
propositions.quote: the female claimant replied that she is not familiar with that organization and that she has no idea what it is about...the claimants did not file a complaint about the alleged threats

propositions.text: Claimants must exhaust all recourse offered by their country before claiming refugee protection in Canada.
propositions.quote: prior to claiming refugee protection in Canada, the female claimant and her husband were required to exhaust all the recourse offered by their country and they neglected to do so.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant was unfamiliar with the ombudsman and did not file complaints; claimants must exhaust local recourse before seeking refugee protection.

propositions.text: Claimants did not use available resources in Israel before leaving.
propositions.quote: Given that the claimants did not use the resources that were available in Israel before leaving

propositions.text: The claimants' problems do not constitute persecution.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the claimants' problems do not constitute persecution

propositions.text: Evidence is insufficient to establish fear of return or risk to life.
propositions.quote: the evidence submitted by the claimants is insufficient to establish a fear of returning to their country and a risk to their life.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimants did not use available resources, their problems are not persecution, and evidence is insufficient to show fear or risk.

propositions.text: Claimants did not show serious possibility of persecution on Convention grounds if returned to Israel.
propositions.quote: the claimants did not demonstrate that there is a "serious possibility" that they would be persecuted under one of the Convention grounds

propositions.text: Claimants did not show on balance of probabilities they would face torture, risk to life, or cruel treatment if returned.
propositions.quote: They also did not demonstrate, on a balance of probabilities, that, should they return to Israel, they would be personally subjected to a danger of torture or to a risk to their life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimants failed to prove serious persecution or risk of torture or cruel treatment if returned to Israel.

propositions.text: The claimants' refugee protection claims are rejected.
propositions.quote: Their claims for refugee protection are rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimants' refugee protection claims.
